label: v362
changes: Timeline qualifications and school reports now carry their linked certificates and documents through to the timeline.
Select a single document card or record title to open its file. Grouped chapters let you choose a moment; records with several attachments show each file.
Document opening works from expanded timelines as well as the normal timeline and All records view.

label: v361
changes: Build my timeline can read saved profile and vault documents, or a PDF / Word CV, and offer work, education and other moments for review before adding them.

Document imports retain source evidence, flag possible duplicates, preserve month/year precision and let you keep a moment without a date. A reading report identifies files or pages that could not be read.
Work is now available in family profiles, with career history, CVs and a place to link or upload work documents. Saved roles appear in the timeline under Work.
Fixed PDF reader loading and increased family CV uploads to 20 MB using file storage. Business CVs retain their existing record-level access and size limit.

label: v360
changes: Life timelines now show intermediate year labels; select a year to explore it, or switch to Scroll to see every year.
Work and School filters stay available. Education now surfaces saved profile and vault certificates, including undated uploads, with an option to add qualification details without uploading again.
Linked certificates appear once in the timeline. Printed document dates are used where available; unknown achievement dates remain clearly undated.

label: v359
changes: Life keeps your full recorded lifespan visible when categories or search hide earlier moments. Switching people uses that person’s own history.
Choose Fit screen for compact, grouped cards or Scroll for full-size cards across Life, Year and Month. Empty years stay available to explore.

Shopping and pickups from older Google Calendar imports no longer appear as medical history. New imports are no longer all labelled appointments. Categories you confirm in the calendar take precedence.

label: v357
changes: The timeline now has Life, Year and Month views. See the whole recorded lifespan on one line, then open a year or month for more detail.
Choose which kinds of moments to show, search the timeline, and expand it for a wider view on a phone, tablet or laptop. Imports, photos and the full records view are still available.
Each family profile has an Education section for school years, teachers, reports, class photos, achievements and qualifications, with links to saved certificates.
Keep previous addresses with move-in and move-out dates. Homes and education records appear in the timeline and relevant exports.

label: v356
changes: Admins can now change how someone's dates are hidden without undoing it first. In Settings, under "Hidden dates", every hidden person has "Change who": pick "Just for me", "Everyone in this family" or "Choose who" and tick exactly who shouldn't see them. The new choice replaces the old one.

"Choose people to hide" now offers "Choose who" to admins too, so you can hide several people from chosen accounts at once. A person who is already hidden has "Change who" on their card as well, so the card is never a dead end.
If a change only half saves, the person stays hidden from more people rather than fewer, and the row tells you what's still hidden so you can try again.

label: v355
changes: Admins can now hide someone's dates from chosen people only. When you tap "Hide <name>'s dates", pick "Choose who" and tick the people who shouldn't see them, other admins included. Everyone you don't tick keeps seeing the birthday, name day and anniversaries as before, in the calendar, in reminders and in their own calendar links.

In Settings, under "People whose dates you've hidden", an admin sees who each person is hidden from, with "Change who" and "Show again". Someone who has had a date hidden from them sees "Hidden for you by the family" there, so a missing birthday is never a mystery. An admin who was ticked can choose "Show for me".

label: v354
changes: You can now hide someone's dates. On a person's profile, their birthday on the calendar, or a relative's row, tap "Hide <name>'s dates": their birthday, name day and anniversaries stop showing on the calendar, the home screen, in reminders and in your calendar link. Nothing is deleted.

Choose who it's for: "Just for me" (the default) hides them only on your account, and "Everyone in this family" hides them for everybody. Children and view-only members can hide people just for themselves.

Settings has a new "People whose dates you've hidden" list. Tap "Show again" to bring someone back, or "Choose people to hide" to pick several at once. When anyone is hidden, the calendar shows a short "2 people's dates hidden · Manage" line, so a missing birthday is never a mystery.

Events from Google Calendar follow the same rule: "Klara's birthday" disappears when Klara is hidden, but "Dinner with Klara" stays. The assistant won't bring up a hidden person's dates by itself, but still answers if you ask.
Fixed: saving Family Settings (for example a new family photo) could quietly remove other settings, including calendars you had subscribed to. Saving now keeps everything it didn't change.

label: v353
changes: Important appointments now stand out. Medical appointments are marked important automatically, and any other event can be marked important with the new Important switch when you add or edit it (the same switch turns the mark off). Important events show a star on the calendar and an Important label on the person's Medical tab.
A new "Important — coming up" card on the home screen lists everything important in the next 30 days: who it's for and how many days to go, soonest first.

Real reminders for important events. When one goes to Google Calendar from Teluva, or reaches another calendar through a Teluva calendar link, it now carries reminders the day before and 2 hours before (all-day events: 9:00 the day before). Busy-only calendar links never carry them.
You can tell the assistant "mark my appointment as important" or "that one isn't important", and when you ask what's coming up it starts with the important ones.

label: v352
changes: Every person now has their own timeline, and the family has one too. Open someone's profile and tap Timeline: the moments you've added about them sit alongside what Teluva already knows — the day they were born, trips on the calendar, dated letters and results from their health record, and documents with a date printed on them. On the family timeline, tap a person to see just their story, or a kind of moment (holidays, school, medical…) to narrow it down. Health moments never show in a business space.

Moments can say who they're about, how exact the date is (a day, a month or just a year — no more "1 January" for something that happened sometime in 2019), where it was, how long it lasted, and carry photos. Older moments whose title starts with someone's name offer a one-tap "About Mia? Tag" — nothing is tagged without that tap.

Import dates. Paste a list, or choose a spreadsheet (CSV, including Austrian semicolon exports), a calendar file (.ics) or a PDF with text in it. Spreadsheets and calendar files are read on your device; only lines Teluva can't read by itself go to the assistant, and it tells you when that happens. You check every row before anything is added — dates already on the timeline, rows without a date and yearly birthdays start unticked — and Undo takes the whole import back out.

Appointments now reach your calendar. A scanned appointment letter ("Ihr Termin am…") keeps its date and time, marks the referral as booked and puts the appointment on the calendar under the right person. Typing an appointment date on a referral does the same. Telling the assistant about an appointment now always offers an Add to calendar card.

Google Calendar now catches up when you open the app, instead of only when you visit the Calendar screen, and no longer stops after the first 250 events. If it can't sync quietly you'll see when it last synced and a Refresh button. Specialist appointments (Orthopädie, Psychiatrie and others) that arrive tagged to nobody now ask "whose is this?" with one tap per person.
Two people editing the timeline at the same time no longer overwrite each other, and editing a moment keeps its photos, documents and other details the form doesn't show.

label: v351
changes: The document scanner now outlines the page live while you hold the phone over it, and takes the shot by itself once the outline holds steady. It will not fire on a dark frame, and a page that runs off the edge of the picture is no longer accepted with its bottom cut off — you get the corner editor instead.

Scans come out at the page's true shape, straight, with white paper and crisp text. Before, pages came out noticeably too wide and slightly off their edges; coloured stamps and signatures now keep their colour while the paper is cleaned up.
Scan several pages into one PDF — up to six — and reorder or remove pages before you save. Handy for a three-page invoice or a contract.

On a phone there is also Take with the camera app (sharpest), which uses your phone's own camera for the photo and then straightens and cleans it the same way. And if you have already scanned something with your iPhone (Notes or Files) or a Mac (Preview), Upload the PDF brings it straight in.

label: v350
changes: Bikes, e-bikes, scooters and motorbikes now live under Vehicles, each with its own icon. Tell it what the thing is first and the form fits it: a bicycle has no number plate, vignette or §57a date to ask about, and its frame number takes the place of a VIN. Vehicles you already have are cars, exactly as before — nothing was changed on them.

Every service and repair entry can now keep its receipt. On a vehicle's service log or the house's Work done list, tap Attach receipt or invoice: scan it, choose a file, or pick something already in your Documents. The file is kept in Documents under Financial, named after the job (“Trek FX — service 10 Sep 2026”), and opens straight from the entry.

Appliances get a service history. There is a new Appliance category in Belongings for the dishwasher, the washing machine or the boiler. Log a repair under Work done, choose which appliance it was, and the job and its invoice show on that appliance's own page — written once, visible from both places.
In Documents, a receipt filed with a service now says what it belongs to, e.g. “Filed with Trek FX · service 10 Sep”. Deleting it from Documents leaves the service entry and its details in place.
Fixed: editing an entry in the house's Work done list could quietly drop details the edit form did not show. Every field on the entry is now kept when you save.

label: v349
changes: Teluva can now file documents out of your email. A small script runs inside your own Gmail, finds the photos and PDFs attached to your mail, and files them in the vault — while you carry on doing nothing. It never reads the text of your messages: only the attachment, who sent it, and the subject line ever leave your mailbox.

Why it works this way: Google treats reading a Gmail attachment as a restricted permission, and an app that asks for it has to pass a paid annual security audit. A script running in your own account does not, so that is where the reading happens. Documents → File documents from your email → Connect Gmail gives you the key; the setup steps live in apps-script/teluva-gmail-bridge/README.md.

The key is shown once and never again. Teluva keeps only a fingerprint of it, so nobody reading the database can recover a working key. Creating a new one immediately stops the old one, and Disconnect stops it altogether. Only an admin can create or revoke one.

label: v348
changes: Send a document straight into the vault from anywhere on your phone. On Android and ChromeOS, Teluva now appears in the system share sheet: open a photo, a scan or a PDF in any app, tap Share, pick Teluva, and the upload form opens already holding it. Apple does not offer this on the iPhone — the two below are the answer there.
Drag a file onto the Documents screen and drop it. Anywhere on the screen works, not just a small target, and the upload form opens holding what you dropped.
Paste a document. Copy a file in Finder or Explorer, or copy an image from anywhere, then press paste with the Documents screen open. Typing into the search box still pastes into the search box.

Groundwork for emailing documents in: forward an email and have its attachments filed in your vault automatically. The whole pipeline is built and tested, and where it is switched on the Documents screen shows your family's own forward-to address with a Copy button. It stays hidden until then — it needs a mail domain, which Teluva does not have yet.

label: v347
changes: The document thumbnails on the ID & Passports tab were drawing their own border inside the tile that already had one, which showed as a doubled edge with a sliver of background at each corner. Same release as the thumbnails themselves — this is the finish on them.

label: v346
changes: Your documents are now shown as documents. The ID & Passports tab opened straight into a wall of text fields, with the scans themselves reduced to a 30-pixel square beside a label. There is now a Documents on file panel at the top of the tab: every passport page, ID card and permit you have scanned for that person, as a real thumbnail you can tap to open full-screen.

Fixed: thumbnails that showed as a broken-image icon. A document scanned through the app's own two-sided flow is saved as a PDF, and thirteen places on the ID & Passports tab were rendering document files as if they could only ever be photographs — so the documents most likely to be there, filed the way the app itself files them, were exactly the ones that appeared torn. The proof-of-address thumbnail on a person's overview had the same fault.

The one-screen ID list now shows the documents too. Alongside every identity number, passport, visa and permit, it lists every document filed for that person with a thumbnail, and marks which number each scan belongs to — so a combined ID and driver's licence photo shows up once, against both.

The Manage connected families window no longer opens a household on its own. It was expanding whenever exactly one family was connected, which meant the same screen behaved differently depending on how many links you happened to have. It now starts collapsed every time, like the card on the profiles screen already did.

label: v345
changes: The scanner now processes what it photographs. Until now a captured page went straight from the camera to storage with no tone correction at all, which is why a birth certificate came out grey and flat next to the same page done in Adobe Scan. Scans now get shadow removal (the lighting gradient across the page is estimated and divided out, so the paper is white on the shady side too), a black and white point set from the page's own histogram, and a light sharpening pass. There is a Colour / Grey / B&W / Original picker on the review screen, and Original is a true bypass that stores exactly what the camera saw.

Better corner detection on the shots that were getting it wrong. The old detector finds edges by contrast, so a pale document on a pale desk gave it a quad that was close but not right — and a quad that is close but wrong is worse than none, because the page is then stretched to fit it. That is what the distorted scans were. A second, model-based detector now runs on any shot the first one is not confident about. It is only downloaded when it is actually needed, so a well-lit page is as fast as before.

You can rotate a scan. A document photographed from the side had no way to be turned, ever. Rotate left and right on the review screen, applied to the original capture rather than stacked on the last rotation, so turning a page four times costs nothing in quality.

Scans are stored at higher resolution. They were compressed to a fixed size and quality chosen so the very worst case would fit under the sync limit, which meant every scan paid for the worst one. Each scan now keeps as much resolution and quality as the limit allows — and a scan that does not fit is compressed further instead of being thrown away with a message asking you to photograph it again.

The assistant can now read medical, health and insurance documents, and search finds scans as well. These were held back deliberately; the rule that it quotes what a document says and never interprets a result or advises on cover is unchanged.

Fixed: a document the app said it could not read a single word of. Pages that came back from OCR with lower confidence — which is what a photograph of a plastic card scores, because it is curved and glossy rather than illegible — had their text deleted before you saw it. You were told the page was blank about a card you can read at arm's length. That text now comes through. A second reading model also now runs on any page the first one finds nothing on, which is the case for ID cards and licences.

Fixed: a passport saved before the app supported more than one was invisible to the assistant and to the new ID-numbers screen. The number was in your records the whole time and every screen that exists to show it said there was none.

Every ID and document number for one person, on one screen. Open it from the ID & Passports tab: identity numbers, passports, visas and permits, each with its expiry, and one button to copy the lot with names attached.
Connected families now start collapsed. A single linked household was being auto-expanded on every visit.

label: v344
changes: The copy button on an ID-number card now takes the name with it, even when there is only one number. Copying gave you the bare digits and nothing else, so a card showing a single ID number had no way at all to copy whose it was — you got "2110056029083" with no Mia attached to it.

There are still two copy controls, and they do different jobs. The small button beside a number copies just that number, which is what you want when filling in a form field. The button in the card header copies the name, what the number is, and the number itself, as one block you can paste into a message. That second button used to appear only when there were two or more numbers; it is now always there.

label: v343
changes: You can now ask which of your documents mentions something, instead of having to name the document first. “Which document has the boiler model?” or “find anything about the notice period” searches the text of everything you have filed and shows you the matching lines, word for word, with the document name and page number.

The search runs on your own device. Your documents' text is read once, kept on that device, and matched there — the query and the passages never go to a server or to the assistant, and the assistant never sees what was found. That also means searching costs nothing, so trying a different word is free.

It tells you what it could not search. Scans and photos have no readable text until they are opened properly, so the results say how many were searched by name only, how many would not load, and how many are outside what the assistant is allowed to look at. “Nothing found” means very little without that.

Every result has a “Read this one properly” link into the full document reader, which reads a whole document page by page including scans. The search finds the document; the reader answers the question.
Medical and health documents are excluded from the search, exactly as they already are from the document reader.

label: v342
changes: The ID-number card now groups by person, and has a Copy all button. Asking about two people used to give you a flat list where every row began with the same name — on a phone that pushed the part saying WHICH number off the end, so two rows both read "Ben Clark's national ID nu…". Now the name is a heading and each number sits under it.

Copy all copies names and numbers together, as one block you can paste straight into a message. The button beside each individual number still copies just that number, which is what you want when filling in a form field — the two do different jobs.
Every copy button now shows a tick when it has worked. A copy changes nothing on screen, so until now the only way to know whether the tap registered was to go and paste it somewhere.

label: v341
changes: Ask the assistant for a passport or ID number and it now shows you the number, instead of telling you it is saved somewhere you should go and look. It appears on its own card under the reply, with a copy button.

How that works matters, because the number is still never sent to the AI. The assistant is shown a list of what you have on file — "Ben's passport number (South Africa)" — and nothing more; when it decides that is what you asked for, it points at the entry and your own device looks the value up and prints it. The AI never sees a digit of it, before or after, and the number is not saved into the conversation either — reopen the chat and it is gone.

Bank account and routing numbers, door and alarm codes, the Wi-Fi password and the free-text Important Numbers stay unreadable to the assistant. Those open something rather than identify someone, which is a different question. Social security and tax IDs from the secure vault are shown to family admins only, matching the screen they live on.

label: v340
changes: The assistant's replies were unreadable in dark mode. The reply bubble kept a near-white background while the text on it turned near-white too, so every answer arrived as a faint smudge. The same fault was making seventeen other things disappear in dark mode — the photo-viewer buttons, the gallery arrows and several date chips — all for one reason: a dark-mode correction that only recognised a fully opaque white, and missed every slightly-see-through one.

label: v339
changes: A colleague's CV can now be exported. Ask the assistant for someone's work history — "put together Katharina's CV and qualifications" — and the folder now carries the real thing: summary, every role with dates, education, certificates with their expiry dates, skills and languages, plus the filed CV file itself. Until now the structured CV facts had no export route at all, and the CV document only travelled inside the blanket "every filed document" option, which brings everything else with it.

The filed CV no longer hides in plain sight. It has to be filed under the generic "Other" category — the document categories have no CV value — so it sat in the Documents list indistinguishable from any uncategorised scan. It now carries a "Filed CV" badge. It stays in the list rather than being hidden, because its delete and share buttons live there and nowhere else.

The CV export finds that file by its identity, not its category. Sweeping up everything filed as "Other" would have put whatever else was in that bucket — an unrelated scan, a random note — into a folder labelled as somebody's CV. A test now files a decoy "Other" document first, so that shortcut fails loudly if anyone reaches for it later.

label: v338
changes: Compliance's country-specific registration terms actually apply now. v337 shipped the right terms for each country — Firmenbuchnummer for Austria, CIPC for South Africa, Companies House for the UK — and wired the space's country in from Business Settings down through two components, but the one line that hands it to the screen that draws the empty state never passed it. Every business kept seeing the generic fallback regardless of country. Caught by checking the live build rather than trusting the green tests, which couldn't see it: the prop is optional, so nothing failed to compile.

label: v337
changes: The nightly reminder digest no longer names a colleague to the whole company. It collects passport, residence-permit, and check-up deadlines for everyone in the space, then sends one push a night. In a business space that push named an employee and stated a fact off their HR file — "Katharina Moser's Austrian passport expires in 7 days" — to every phone on the team, the same disclosure v330 closed in the sign-in rules and v333 closed for birthdays. It went unnoticed because the celebrations send twenty lines above it already had the business/family split; this one didn't. Personal deadlines now reach the people who already hold the file; a shared calendar entry — tomorrow's site inspection — still reaches everyone.

A lapsing certificate now actually sends a reminder. The CV tab has drawn an "Expires soon" chip on a first-aid certificate or a driving licence since it shipped, and the AI offers to remind you about one — but the nightly job that sends reminders never read that list. It does now.

Re-scanning a CV that's already on file stops reporting a change that didn't happen. The assistant merges an incoming CV against what's already saved — a role or qualification already on record is dropped, not duplicated — but the confirmation card was built from the raw scan, so it said "2 roles, 1 qualification" and then applied none of them. The card now counts what will actually land.

A colleague's work summary is on their profile page, not one click further in. Opening a team member's profile in a business space showed nothing about who they are at work until you opened the CV tab specifically. Their current role and next-expiring certificate are on the landing screen now.

Compliance stops assuming every business is South African. "No numbers yet" and its placeholder suggested CIPC, SARS, UIF and COIDA regardless of where the business is registered; an Austrian company now sees Firmenbuchnummer and UID, a UK one sees Companies House and PAYE.

Three smaller wording leaks in Compliance: the contacts form pointed at "Extended Birthdays" and "the family calendar", a view a business space doesn't have; the provider "for" field still said "blank = whole family" even in a business space; and the household vendors list — the plumber, the electrician, reachable in both kinds of space — never re-labelled itself for one.

A date badge no longer sits on top of the fourth person's portrait on a phone. The home screen's family scene overlapped by 83 pixels at 375px wide; the portraits now shrink before they reach the badge's corner.

label: v336
changes: The Team screen no longer white-screens for an employee. Opening it in a business space blanked the entire app — not the section, the whole thing — for anyone who is not an owner. The screen carries a short note explaining that colleagues' records stay private, and the padlock icon beside that note was never imported. "Lock" also happens to be the name of a browser feature, so the code compiled, the type checker passed it, and the app only fell over when it tried to draw it. It has been broken since the employee view shipped, and the first person to meet it would have been a new employee on their first day.

Every icon in the app is now checked against this. The reason that one slipped through is that the missing name existed anyway — as something else entirely. A test now walks every screen and fails if anything is drawn that was never imported, so the next name that collides with a browser feature is caught before it ships rather than by whoever opens the screen.

The welcome tour stops describing a family to a company. Its closing slide promised a family quiz, a growing-up video, a recipe book and a travel timeline — all four of which a business space hides. It pointed at Wills & Estate, also hidden, and at "Household", which is called Locations there. And it suggested trying "add a dentist visit for Mia on the 12th". A business now gets its own wording throughout, and a test renders every step in both kinds of space and fails on anything named that the space does not have.

Seven more places were telling a business it was a family. The signed-out vault card offered to "use this space with your own family", the home screen said "Open People" when that section is called Team, Operations talked about "the home record", filing a document offered "Whole family", and the placeholders suggested "e.g. Family car" and "e.g. Household, Mia". All of them now read correctly, and the family wording is untouched.

The team list is readable again for whoever runs the space. An owner gets a drag handle and a delete button on every row, and with those present the name column collapsed to about the width of one word — "Katharina Moser" rendered as "Katl". It only affected owners, which is why it survived: the public demo has no account, so nobody browsing casually was ever shown it.

The public demo can now show a business. Until now the only way to see a business space was to buy one, and the demo — having no account — quietly showed the employee's half of a company you own, with Finances and Insurance missing from the menu. It opens as the owner now, and adding &as=employee to the address shows the other side deliberately.

label: v335
changes: Attaching a photo while editing a trip now reads its location, the same as adding one does. The "add a trip" button has detected the country from a photo's GPS data since the feature shipped; the edit form never did — it re-encoded the photo first, which strips the location data off it, and then had nothing left to read. So the screen promising automatic detection was telling the truth on one path and not the other.

Changing a trip's country no longer leaves the old country's flag on it. Renaming a trip from Austria to France kept Austria's country code underneath, so the entry showed an Austrian flag beside the word France, still counted Austria in your countries-visited total, and kept a pin at the old coordinates. All three came from the same place and all three are now cleared when you change the name.

And it stops calling a trip "Auto-tagged" once you have typed the country yourself. That badge means the app worked it out from the photo. If you overrule it, it says Manual, because that is what happened.

A photo that disagrees with what you typed now asks instead of overwriting. If the country box is empty it just fills it in; if you have already written something, the photo's answer appears as an offer with a button. A photo taken on the drive home genuinely belongs to a different country than the trip does, and you are the one who knows which you meant.

One honest limit: the offline country lookup does not recognise every way of writing a country's name — "Netherlands", "Denmark", "Ireland", "China" and "United States" among them. Those entries simply show no flag. A missing flag is only less decoration; the wrong flag was a lie, and that is the one we have removed.

label: v334
changes: The home screen now tells you what changed. A new card, "Recently changed", lists what has been added, updated or removed in this vault and who did it — newest first. Until now the vault could be edited by five people and looked identical afterwards, so the only way to notice a change was to already know where to look.

You only see entries for things you can already open. A child sees the shared things; an adult sees those plus finances and documents; an owner sees everything including passwords and Wills & Estate. A shorter list is not a fault — it is the same boundary the rest of the app uses, applied to the record of changes as well.

It records that something changed, never what it changed to. "A password was updated" — not which one, and never the value. The entries for passwords and the will are deliberately unnamed even for the owner, because a list of which passwords changed this week is itself worth stealing.

Nobody can edit the list afterwards, not even an owner. That is what makes it worth checking when something looks wrong. It is not an audit log and the app will not call it one: the app writes the entries, so an entry can be missing — what it cannot be is forged or quietly rewritten.
Entries are kept for 60 days and then deleted. Long enough to answer "what did I miss", short enough that the vault is not also keeping a permanent history of everyone's habits.

This is not a news feed, and there is still no posting, liking or commenting anywhere in Teluva. That was a real question and this is the honest answer to it: a vault that asks for the family's most private records should not also be a place where people perform for each other.

label: v333
changes: The company's bank details are now owners-only. In a business space the finances document — banks, IBANs, insurance policies, benefits — was readable by every employee. The rule behind it said "adults, not children", which is exactly right in a household and means something entirely different at work.

A colleague's birthday is no longer announced to the whole team. In a family, telling everyone it's someone's birthday is the point. In a business it publishes a named employee's date of birth to their colleagues, and in Austria that needs the person's own consent, not the employer's decision. Owners still get the reminder, so you can still wish someone happy birthday — it just doesn't go out to everybody.
The business's own anniversary is not personal and still reaches everyone.

Two switches that were being ignored now work. "No fuss, please" on a person, and the space-wide celebrations switch: the app has respected both for months, and the thing that actually sends the notifications had never read either. If you turned celebrations off, you were still being buzzed.

Turning them off no longer hides anyone from the calendar. Opting out of being congratulated is not opting out of appearing on the day, so the dates are still worked out and still shown — only the notification stops.

A start date has been taken back off the team directory. It went in last week on the reasoning that work anniversaries were already announced team-wide. They are not — they are worked out on your own phone from the people you can see. Nothing had published it, and the directory would have been the first thing to.

label: v332
changes: Business spaces get a team directory. Last week's change made a colleague's record an HR file — right, and it left "Your team" holding one person, which reads less like a boundary than a broken app. The directory is the other half: who works here, what they do, and the work number to reach them on.

Work contact only, and the list is fixed on the server rather than chosen by the app. Name, job title, work phone, work address, start date. Personal numbers, home addresses, birthdays, ID numbers and medical details are not on that list and cannot be added by anything running on a phone.

Two things are missing on purpose. A colleague's birthday and a colleague's photo both need that person's consent under Austrian law, not just an employer's decision, and this app has nowhere to record consent yet — so neither is shown, and the screen says so rather than leaving you to notice.
The rows do not open anything. There is no profile behind them for this account to read, and a row that leads to a permission error is worse than a row that simply gives you the number.
Owners and admins are unchanged and still see full records.

label: v331
changes: Asking to read the will now actually tells the admins. The screen has said since last week that every admin is told straight away and can refuse — nothing was being sent. On a mechanism where seven days of silence opens the will, an owner who is never told has a theoretical chance to refuse rather than a real one.

Two surfaces, deliberately. A notification goes to every admin's phone the moment somebody asks; and the request also appears at the top of the home screen, under Needs attention, counting down, until it is refused or it opens. Notifications are the surface that quietly fails — permission never granted, switched off, a new phone — so the one that cannot fail is the home screen.

The notification goes to admins only, and only to devices it can match to an admin. A phone the vault cannot identify gets nothing, which is the opposite of how ordinary family notifications work here and is the right way round for a message about somebody's will.
Only an admin sees the countdown row, because only an admin can refuse. Telling anyone else would be telling them about a request they cannot act on, to open a document they cannot read.

label: v330
changes: Business spaces: a colleague's record is now treated as an HR file, not a family profile. In a business space an employee can open their own record and nobody else's. Owners and admins are unaffected and still see everyone.

This closes something real. Business spaces reused the family's access model, where every adult can read every other — which is exactly right in a household and means, in a business, that any employee could open any colleague's medical details, home address and date of birth. The Owner/Manager/Employee labels on a profile looked like permissions; they are text, and they granted nothing.

The change is in the database rules, not in what the app chooses to show. Hiding a screen protects nothing — the rule is the only thing that counts, and it is now proven by 53 checks run against the real rules engine.

An employee sees a short note explaining why their team list holds only them, rather than being left to conclude the app is broken. A proper team directory — name, job title and work contact, separated from the confidential fields — is the next step, and until it exists the safe answer is the narrow one.

Nothing changes for family spaces. A household genuinely shares these records and every adult reading every other IS the feature; the same rule now simply gives a different answer depending on which kind of space it is asked about.

label: v329
changes: Accepting an estate invite no longer opens the will. Until now, the moment somebody tapped accept they could read the whole Wills & Estate page — while you were alive and well. That was never what the invite said it did, and it is not what anybody assumed it did.

Being named now gives them two things. They can see WHERE THE SIGNED WILL IS — held by a notary, lodged in a register, whatever you have recorded. And they can ask to read the rest, which you are told about and can refuse.

If nobody refuses, the full will opens seven days after they ask. If a second named person also agrees and you have not opened Teluva for fourteen days, it can open sooner. Nothing here decides that anyone has died.
You can still let somebody read it today — one tap on 'Who can open this'. That is now a decision you make, rather than something that happens because an invite was accepted.

IMPORTANT: this changes new invites only. Anyone who ALREADY accepted an estate invite keeps the full access they were given. Open 'Who can open this' on the Wills & Estate page to see exactly who that is, and untick anyone who should not have it yet.

label: v328
changes: A fix on top of yesterday's release: if the app could not reach the vault, the Ask for the will to be opened screen could show an empty, calm 'no requests' instead of saying something had gone wrong. On this screen in particular, a silent blank is the worst possible answer, so it now says plainly that it could not reach the vault.

label: v327
changes: If you are named to help with someone's estate and the will is not open to you yet, the Wills & Estate page no longer just tells you to ask an admin. It now has a button: Ask for the will to be opened. The old advice was sound right up until the person you would have to ask is the person whose will it is.

There are two ways a request opens the will. If a SECOND named person also agrees, it opens straight away — but only if the owner has not opened Teluva for 14 days. If nobody agrees and nobody objects, it opens on its own after 7 days.

The owner sees every request on their own Wills & Estate page and can refuse it with one press. Refusing is final for that request, not a pause — a paused clock the owner thought they had stopped would be worse than no button at all.

Teluva still has NO death detection, and is not getting any. Nothing here decides that somebody has died. Being quiet is only ever permission for two people who already agree to skip the seven-day wait; on its own it opens nothing.
When it does open, BOTH people who agreed can read it — neither has to relay to the other what it says, which is exactly where the arguments start.

label: v326
changes: Someone you have named to help with your estate can now always see WHO HOLDS your signed will — at every sharing level, including the lowest one. This is a deliberate change to what the lowest level means, and it is the only widening this app has made: a will nobody can find is not a protected will, it is a lost one.
What crosses is a custodian — a notary, an office, a named person — or the fact that it is lodged in a register. Knowing a notary in Vienna holds the will does not let anyone take it.

Where a will is physically hidden still stays private, with one exception: if nobody holds it and it is in no register, then where it is kept is the only thing in the world that can find it, so that crosses instead.
If nothing at all has been recorded, the person you named is told that plainly — so they can ask you now, rather than discover it on the day it is too late to ask.
The notary's direct phone line still never crosses, and neither does whether a will is a draft. Being disorganised is not a fact about where a document is.

label: v325
changes: Funeral cover now has its own section on the Wills & Estate page: provider, policy number, who the payout goes to, whether repatriation is included, and the claims number as a button you can press to ring it. It is the first thing a family needs and it used to be three screens away under Insurance.
The number is still only editable under Finances → Insurance, so one policy has one owner and two screens cannot disagree about a claims line.

A policy still inside its waiting period is listed below one that is through, and says so — it may still pay on an accidental death, so it is not hidden, but it is not the number you are handed first either.
The section appears even when nothing is recorded. A funeral card that quietly disappears reads as “there is no cover”, which is the one thing it must never imply.

label: v324
changes: Wills & Estate opens with a readiness bar: how much is recorded, what is still missing, and one plain sentence for each thing still to do. The instructions live inside the steps, so they are there while you work rather than in a preamble you scroll past.
One of those steps exists because a will only takes effect after death. Being alive and unable to decide is a different situation needing different papers, and nothing in the app used to say so.
The step order reflects what actually loses an estate: finding the signed original and recording the funeral claims number outrank tidiness.

The “here is what changed” card after an update is now off by default and can be switched on per device, under Settings. The separate “you are on an old version, tap to refresh” notice still shows for everyone — that one fixes a real problem rather than reporting news.

label: v323
changes: An estate document now records what state it is actually in — unsigned draft, signed copy, or the signed original — plus whether it is in a will register. A Word file nobody printed and a notarised original used to look identical on the list. They no longer do.

Where a will is recorded as signed but nothing says where the original is kept, who holds it, or that it is registered, the app now says so. In Austria the court's notary checks the registers automatically, but only documents held by a notary or lawyer are in them — a will written at home has to be produced by whoever has the paper.
That warning appears only where it is true: never on a draft, and never on a power of attorney or healthcare directive, which are not produced to a probate court.
Fixed: two test suites written this week were never actually being run. Both pass, and a new check now fails the build if any test file is left out again.

label: v322
changes: A shared profile now shows every section their family switched on — Wish list, Sizes, What they like, name days — even when there is nothing in one yet. An empty one says so plainly instead of vanishing and making a working feature look broken.
It only ever says that where the switch is actually on. If a family chose not to share something, the section stays absent and nothing on the screen claims they left it blank.
Name days now appear for any family that has turned them on, and read “none recorded yet” when there are none.
An empty “In your care” tab gets its own wording: nothing written down is not the same as “no allergies”, so it says that outright and tells you to ask them.

label: v321
changes: A connected cousin's profile now has “What they like” — hobbies, colours, music, books, films, games, brands, the food they love and the food they don't. It is the answer to “what do I buy them” when nobody wrote a wish list.
You fill it in on your own people under their Preferences tab, which now says plainly that connected families can read it, and which people it crosses for.

Dietary restrictions are the deliberate exception. They stay out of the gift list and only ever cross if you switch on “In their care” — what someone must avoid can be a diagnosis or a religion, and that is not a present-buying detail.

label: v320
changes: A shared cousin's profile is no longer a name and a birthday. It now shows their star sign — worked out from the birthday you can already see, so it appears exactly when the birthday does and never on its own.

What their name means, where it comes from, and the family surname alongside it. Every meaning carries how sure it is — established, likely or contested — because a name story told as fact about somebody else's family is worse than no story.

Name days can now cross too, but only if a family switches them on. A feast day names a religion, so this one is never assumed: it stays off until the household chooses it, in Connected families → Manage.

Removed the “Not shared” tab. It listed things the other family had not sent, which read as a list of what they were withholding — and it was often wrong, because a family with no wish list looks identical to one that hid it. The profile now says in one line what stays with them and that either side can change it.

label: v319
changes: Open a lease, a contract or any document in ChatGPT, Claude or whatever else is on your phone. It is a labelled button now rather than something hiding behind “Share”, and Teluva says once, in words, that the file is leaving and the other app's rules apply to it from there.

It is offered where the reader stops too: when the app tells you it cannot say whether a clause obliges anybody, it now also hands you the file to take elsewhere — after the list of people actually qualified to answer, not instead of it.
Fixed: a PDF shared out of Teluva could arrive named .jpg and be refused by the receiving app. Documents now keep their real file type.

label: v318
changes: Utilities now hold what you actually need. Electricity and gas ask for two companies, not one: who you pay, and the grid operator who owns the wire or pipe, comes with the address, and is who you ring when it goes off — the number almost nobody has when they need it.

The right fault number is on the card without opening it, as a tap-to-ring link. Where a national one exists the app already knows it — 128 for gas in Austria, 105 for a power cut and 0800 111 999 for gas in Britain. Where there isn't one, it says so instead of guessing.

The bill's two numbers are now two fields that explain themselves: the metering point that belongs to the address and survives a change of supplier (Zählpunktnummer, MPAN, MPRN, POD), and the meter number stamped on the meter that changes when the meter does.
Put in when a contract ends and how much notice it needs, and the app tells you before the window closes — a fixed price rolling onto a standard tariff is the most expensive thing on that page.
Meter readings, with a note of whether you read it, they read it, or it was estimated. Two of your own readings and a date are what an estimated bill can be argued with.
Rows you already had still work exactly as they did, and the assistant can now file all of it by dictation.

label: v317

changes: Tap a connected family's photo to open them as a family — their picture, everyone they share, whose birthday is next, and how much of them you can actually see.

changes: On phones, long section labels (like "People · Important information") no longer run underneath the circular section badge — they wrap clearly beside it.

The Family Calendar's at-a-glance panels — Travel documents, Birthdays, Name days & celebrations, Medical checks, Anniversaries, and School dates — can each be turned on or off from Settings > Calendar panels.

label: v219
changes: Reopening the guided setup part-way through no longer drops you straight into a bare numbered question — a short welcome-back card now shows what step you left off on, with the choice to continue there or start over.

Added name days and other name-based celebrations. Confirm one from a family member's profile — a name day, a saint's day, a family name connection, or any other tradition tied to someone's name — and it shows up alongside birthdays on the Family Calendar.

label: v218
changes: Moved the vault to a new, properly provisioned database. The old one had a hard daily usage cap that caused yesterday's "couldn't load your account" outage — the new one has no such cap, so that outage can't happen again. All your data came across unchanged.

label: v217
changes: Fixed a bug where a brief connection hiccup while signing in could send an existing account to a "set up your family vault" screen instead of their real vault. It now shows a plain "couldn't load your account, try again" message instead — never a screen that looks like you need to start from scratch.

label: v216
changes: The guided setup now shows a visible progress bar and a colour-coded icon for what each question is about — medical, emergency contact, documents, and so on — instead of a plain grey "Question N of 30".

label: v215
changes: New: Gifts & Occasions — everyone's upcoming birthdays, name days and Christmas in one place, with their wishlist right there so you know what to get and where.

label: v214
changes: The address proof-of-document link on a member's Overview tab is now a small thumbnail too, matching ID & Passports — tap it to see the full scan.

label: v213
changes: ID & Passports now has one way to view a saved scan instead of three — tap the small thumbnail next to any passport or ID field to see the full document.

label: v212
changes: Saved scans now show the whole document instead of a tight, zoomed-in crop — the scanner requires a much better-framed shot before it will accept a page as done.

label: v211
changes: The Family calendar now puts planning first with a clearer month-and-agenda layout, month-by-month reminders for the next six months, and a permanent travel-document watch for passport, visa and residence-card renewals. Calendar connections stay one click away, and duplicate reviews now sit neatly with the Google tools they belong to.

label: v210
changes: Health timeline is no longer just for kids: open it for anyone in the family from their Medical tab, and see vaccinations, check-ups, referrals & results and appointments all merged into one history alongside growth — plus blood group, allergies and other essentials always shown at the top.

label: v209
changes: AI Chat: your reply now saves even if you close the chat panel while it's still working — no more losing an answer or a scan result because you switched away too soon.

label: v208
changes: Document Scanner: fixed the capture-review and crop-adjust screens getting cut off with no way to scroll down to Save on short/phone screens.
Document Scanner: the camera no longer auto-captures a dark/black shot while it's still adjusting to light — it now waits and tells you to move to better light instead.

label: v207
changes: Calendar: birthdays, passport/visa renewals, and appointments you've added yourself now show above anything imported from a connected Google Calendar, in both the day view and the upcoming-reminders list.

label: v206
changes: Fixed: the document scanner could get stuck taller than the screen on phones, hiding the "Use this side" / "Save as PDF" button and the crop tool below the visible area with no way to scroll down to them.

label: v204
changes: Fixed: ID numbers (SSN, driver's licence, tax ID, insurance number) and bank account/routing numbers entered under Secure Secrets were being stored without encryption, even though the panel was labelled "Stored locally." Both are now encrypted at rest, the same as passwords and other credentials in that section, and the label now says so correctly.

label: v203
changes: Fixed: two devices saving around the same time could silently overwrite each other's family member or calendar changes — a passport scanned on one phone could vanish minutes later because of an unrelated save on another. Every save now merges field-by-field against the current cloud copy instead of overwriting it whole.
Fixed: visa numbers were being stored in plain text and sent to the assistant unredacted — now encrypted at rest and withheld from AI chat, matching passports and other ID numbers.
Fixed: the assistant's "what's coming up" heads-up was missing overdue care visits, unbooked referrals, and lapsed funeral cover.
Fixed: the calendar the assistant sees for "what's coming up" could fill up with far-future events and miss things happening this week.

Fixed: if you asked the assistant to update a family member's info and the name was ambiguous or didn't match anyone, it could silently apply to the wrong person or mark itself done having changed nothing. It now tells you when it couldn't tell who you meant, and skips instead of guessing.
Fixed: assistant edits or deletions to a referral, vehicle, or similar record could silently do nothing without saying why.
Fixed: Undo now correctly warns when a deleted or directly-edited record from an assistant change can't be restored, instead of staying silent about it.
Fixed: dismissing a suggested change in AI chat could reappear after a refresh; starting a new chat could leave old "Applied"/duplicate markers showing on the first message of the new one.
Fixed: if part of a batch of assistant changes failed to save partway through, retrying could quietly save some of it twice — you're now pointed to Undo first instead.
Removed a leftover "alarm code" field the assistant's instructions mentioned but the app never actually had.

label: v202
changes: New: Namenstag (name day). If your name has one in the Austrian calendar, your profile now offers it — tap once to keep it, and it shows up on the home screen and in your daily notification alongside birthdays. Nothing is guessed for a name the calendar doesn't recognise, and you can also set or correct one by hand on the Edit profile screen.

Fixed: someone removed from a family (or who left one) kept getting that family's birthday and reminder notifications on their phone indefinitely. Their device is now dropped from the notification list the moment they leave.

Fixed: opening the document reader from the Document Vault (rather than from chat) could spin forever on a slow connection with no way back except closing the screen. It now gives up gracefully after three minutes, same as chat.
Fixed: Household and Finances could flip to showing raw encrypted text on screen after a change synced in from another device or family member.
Fixed: someone born on 29 February never got a birthday notification in an ordinary year.
Fixed: two celebrations landing on the same day (two birthdays, or a birthday and a name day) could silently cancel each other out as a notification.
Fixed: birthdays, passport/permit expiry and other date-only reminders synced to Google Calendar as a 9am meeting instead of an all-day event.
Fixed: the assistant can now update or delete a visa, vaccination or referral record it filed, and Undo now covers those too.

Fixed: a few smaller things — a retry button on a timed-out document read that didn't do anything, a free-text "Important Numbers" value that was being sent to the AI unnecessarily, an emoji in a calendar export that could corrupt the file, photo-measurement readings not counting against the monthly AI limit, and the document reader charging an AI action on a search that never reached the AI.

label: v201
changes: Asking a second question about the same document is now much faster. Your phone was re-scanning every page of the document from scratch on every single question — the slowest part of the whole thing — to produce pages the server had already read and saved. It now checks first, and skips straight to the answer.
This is what made a read time out and give up on a long scanned lease, even though the answer was ready.

label: v200
changes: Asking about a document now actually opens it. The same file is stored under two different internal ids — one in the shared vault, one on the person's profile — and the assistant kept naming the profile one, which the reader didn't recognise. That is why "I'll check your Home Lease Agreement" was followed by nothing at all. Both forms now resolve.

label: v199
changes: The document reader was giving up 20 seconds in — and hiding it. Reading a lease properly takes about 45 seconds; past 20 the app quietly abandoned the read and showed you a plain word search instead, laid out exactly like a real answer. That is why a question about repairs came back as three paragraphs about storm insurance. The limit now matches how long the work actually takes.
If a read ever does fall back, the app says so on screen and offers to read it properly, instead of presenting a word search as the answer.
Fixed the "answered by an earlier version of the reader" note appearing on brand-new answers. It was showing on every single read, which made the one notice that matters worthless.

label: v198
changes: Asking about a document is more reliable. The assistant identifies the document by name as well as by its internal id, so a single mistyped digit can no longer leave you with "I'll check your lease" and nothing after it.
When a document read can't be opened, that is now recorded instead of passing silently — so a failure like that can be found and fixed rather than repeating.

label: v197
changes: A document read that never finished no longer spins for ever. If the app closed, the connection dropped, or a long scanned document stalled while it was being read, that message came back as a permanent "Reading…" with no way out — and it stayed that way through every reload. It now says the read didn't finish and gives you a "Try reading it again" button.
Every failed read has a way forward. Previously a read that errored was a dead end: no answer, and nothing on screen that could go and get it.

label: v196
changes: The assistant and the document reader now run on a stronger model. Tested on a real 9-page lease, the old one got 9 of 13 questions right and the new one got all 13 — including the German question it used to give up on entirely, and the ones where it wrongly said "the lease does not cover that". Answers take a few seconds longer and are shorter and more specific.
An old answer in your chat now has an "Ask this again" button, so a reply given before an improvement can be re-asked without retyping it.

label: v195
changes: An old answer in your chat now has an "Ask this again" button. When the reader has been improved since an answer was given, the note that says so no longer just tells you to retype the question — it re-sends the question you originally asked, through today's reader.

label: v194
changes: Asking about a document now sends your whole question, not one word out of it. "Under what conditions can I call an electrician or plumber for repairs" was being cut down to "conditions" before the reader ever saw it — so it answered the keyword instead of the question. It now reads your question as you asked it.

The list of words it searched for is readable again. It was showing you its internal spelling guesses — "coenditioens", "pluember" — which is a poor look on the one screen where it tells you it found nothing. It still searches for every spelling; it just no longer pretends they are words.

label: v193
changes: A finished document read stops saying it's still reading. The line above the answer was written the moment the search started and never updated, so every answer in your chat — including ones from weeks ago — claimed to be happening right that second. It now reads in the past tense once the search is done.

Changing the app's language now reaches the document reader. The reader was being handed whichever language was set when the chat first opened, so switching afterwards left answers and translations in the old one until you reloaded.

label: v192
changes: An old answer no longer passes itself off as a current one. Your chat keeps every document answer it has ever given, and they are re-drawn by whatever version of the app you're running now — so an answer from before a fix looked exactly like one given today. Older ones now say so, and tell you to ask again.
The reader itself is unchanged in this release. Ask a document question again and you get today's reader: the answer up top, the clauses it came from underneath, translated into your language.

label: v191
changes: Passports can hold a photo of the page. When you add or edit a passport there's now a "Take photo" button that opens the camera straight away, and a "Choose file" next to it. The page appears as a thumbnail on the passport, and tapping it opens it full-size — which is the thing a consulate asks for when a passport goes missing abroad, and it carries everything nobody thinks to type in.

The photo is filed as a document, not stuffed into the record. It lands in that person's Documents like any other scan, so it syncs, exports and shares the same way — and a passport that already had a scan filed under it still finds it.

label: v190
changes: It no longer tells you something isn't in your document. It cannot know that — a figure left blank on a printed form, a handwritten amount, a page that scanned poorly and a genuinely silent contract all look identical from the inside. So it now says what it found and, where it came up short, that it couldn't find it and you should check the page yourself.

It flags contradictions instead of picking a side. Your lease says in one place that dogs are absolutely fine and in another that pets are prohibited. Both now come back, side by side, rather than whichever one it happened to read first.
Answers stopped citing numbers you can't see. It was referring to "clause 112" — an internal position in a list that never appears on your screen. It now points at the page instead.

label: v188
changes: Ask about your document and you now get an answer, in your own language — not just a pile of clauses. Teluva reads the relevant parts and tells you plainly where you stand, who to contact and by when, with the document's own words quoted underneath so you can check every word of it.
Foreign-language documents are translated. An Austrian lease, a Spanish contract: each quoted clause appears in the language the app is set to, with the original still shown beneath it.

It now reads the whole document, not just the parts containing your words. Searching for "electrician" used to miss the block with your managing agent's phone number, because that block doesn't contain the word — it just happens to be the most useful thing on the page. Teluva now considers every clause and picks the ones that actually bear on your question.

label: v187
changes: Scanned documents are now read properly — all of them, not one page in nine. Teluva was handing your whole PDF to Google to unpack, and on a nine-page lease Google managed exactly one page and rejected the other eight. Teluva now prepares each page itself before sending it, and the same lease reads front to back.

Ask in your own words, get the clause anyway. If nothing in the document contains the words you typed, Teluva now looks for the parts that are about what you asked instead of shrugging. Ask about an electrician and you get the repair and maintenance clauses — clearly labelled as related rather than as matches, so you know which is which.

A page with text and a page that's a photo can now live in the same document. Teluva reads the text pages as text and the scanned pages as pictures, instead of giving up on the whole file because one page happened to have a text layer.

label: v186
changes: Teluva can now read scanned documents. Most of what a family actually keeps is a photo or a scan — a lease off the copier, an insurance letter photographed on the kitchen table — and until now Teluva could only read documents that were born as digital text. Ask about a scanned lease and you now get the clause back, quoted, with its page number.

It tells you when it read from a picture rather than from text. Passages from a scan carry a "read from an image" tag, because reading ink off a photograph is a different kind of certainty to reading a text file — and Teluva still will not tell you your document doesn't say something, since a word it misread looks exactly like a word that was never there.
A page it couldn't make out is named, not skipped. If three pages of a nine-page scan are too blurred to read, it says which three rather than quietly searching the other six and calling it done.
Reading a scan happens once. The result is kept with the document, so every question after the first comes back straight away.

label: v185
changes: The answer now appears in the chat itself. Ask what your lease says about repairs and the clauses come back in the conversation, with page numbers, quoted word for word — no sheet to open, nothing to tap. The document speaks for itself, right where you asked.

Fixed: documents wouldn't load at all on the new address. Teluva's file storage was still only expecting the old web address, so every attempt to read a document failed with "Failed to fetch". Both addresses are now allowed.

When nothing matches, Teluva says exactly that — and says what it searched for, and names any page it couldn't read. It will not tell you your document doesn't mention something, because that is the one thing it has no way to know.

label: v184
changes: Ask about a document and the answer just appears. Before, the assistant offered you a button and waited to be asked a second time; now it opens the document, searches it, and shows you the wording itself. You ask once.

The assistant no longer opens by telling you what it can't do. When a question is about a document, the reply you see is written by Teluva, not by the AI — so "I cannot read the content of the document" can no longer be said about a document Teluva is in the middle of reading for you.

Fixed: an app installed from Teluva's old web address was silently frozen on an old version. Teluva was renamed, the old address kept running, and every update for the past week went to the new one — so an app opened there kept working, kept saying it was up to date, and kept showing an old Teluva. It now recognises the old address and offers to move you across.

label: v174
changes: Long-press (or click) now works on any displayed block of info — chronic conditions, allergies, medications, blood type, emergency contact, employer — not just ID numbers, to Copy or Share it.

That same long-press menu now has a "Scan" option: snap or pick a photo relevant to what you're looking at, and it opens the assistant with that photo already attached and a note about what it's for, ready for you to send.

Tap any item on a family member's Belongings card to see everything on file for it — not just the name, but make/model, serial number, purchase price, warranty, where it's kept, and photos — with an edit form right there if you're an admin.

Fixed: photographing an item you'd already filed (e.g. a medical device) and asking the assistant to update it created a second, duplicate entry instead of correcting the original. The assistant can now see what's already in the inventory and will update the existing item — or ask, if it's genuinely unsure — rather than guess and file a duplicate.
Fixed: a photo attached to an "add this to our things" message was silently dropped — only the text details were saved. The photo is now kept with the item.
You can now also ask the assistant to remove or correct an item in the family inventory by name, the same way you can for passports, vehicles and receipts.

Filled real gaps found in a full audit of what the assistant can set vs. what you can edit yourself: Austria now has fields for ID document type, birth certificate number, and private health insurance number; added a garage code field to Household; added Nationality and Gender to a family member's profile.
Renamed "Sozialversicherungsnummer (SV)" to "Social Security Number (Sozialversicherungsnummer / SV number)" — several people couldn't find it by searching for the English term.

Government ID numbers (SV numbers, passport numbers, tax numbers and the rest), household access codes, and bank details are now encrypted the same way saved passwords always have been — a database copy or leak no longer exposes them in plain text. Security page updated with the details.
Fixed: passport numbers were being sent to the AI assistant along with the question you asked it — they're now held back like every other ID number, only the country and expiry stay visible.
The assistant now asks which number you mean when correcting an SV number or e-card number, instead of guessing — the two look alike but are different fields.
Fixed: the "new version available" banner could go stale if it fired and then more updates shipped while your tab stayed open — it now always shows what's genuinely latest.
The app should feel noticeably snappier — the first load now ships about a third less code, since each screen only downloads when you actually open it instead of all twenty loading up front.
The welcome tour now mentions Calendar sync and Google Drive, and fixed a step that was silently never showing.
You can now join a second family or business space with an invite code from the menu under your family's name, not just the very first time you sign in.
The assistant can now read and update the family status line ("everyone's at Oma's until Sunday") — it could see everything else but not that, until now.
Fixed: a save that failed while you were offline could later be silently overwritten and lost the next time the app reconnected — it's now protected until it actually syncs.

label: v167
changes: Google Drive is now live: tap "Choose from Google Drive" to pick files or a whole folder using Google's own picker window, instead of browsing your Drive inside Teluva. Teluva now only ever sees the files or folder you actually pick, nothing else in your Drive.

label: v166
changes: The chat assistant can now see much more of a large family's history at once before anything gets left out. The old limit was far more cautious than it needed to be for the size of vault this app actually holds.

label: v165
changes: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for Google Drive: the app is now ready to let you pick files or a whole folder using Google's own picker window, rather than browsing your Drive inside Teluva. Nothing changes for you yet — today's folder browser keeps working exactly as it does now until this is switched on.

label: v164
changes: The calendar now spots appointments that were saved twice and offers to tidy them up. You see exactly what would go before anything is removed, and one copy of each is always kept — the one with the most detail on it.
Anything coming from a calendar you subscribed to is left alone, since removing it would only bring it back on the next refresh.
Small fix: the new "show Teluva in your own calendar" section no longer appears with nothing under it while it is still loading.

label: v163
changes: Teluva can now appear inside your own calendar. Create a link in the calendar panel, paste it into Apple Calendar, Outlook or Google as a subscribed calendar, and these events show up alongside everything else and keep themselves up to date.

You choose what the link shows: full details, or busy-only with no titles at all. It can be turned off again at any time, and it only ever carries calendar entries — never documents, IDs or medical records.
Events Teluva brought in from another calendar are never published back out, so nothing bounces around and shows up twice.

label: v162
changes: You can now subscribe to another calendar, not just import from it. Paste the private link Apple, Outlook, Proton or Google gives you and Teluva keeps itself up to date — appointments that move, move, and cancelled ones disappear instead of lingering.

A one-off .ics file import is still there for when you just want a snapshot.

label: v161
changes: The sign-in screen no longer quietly asks Google for permission it doesn't need yet — that only happens once you're actually signed in.
The demo now shows the star-sign card, with one family member who has a full birth time and place so you can see the Sun, Moon and Rising signs it works out.

label: v160
changes: On a calendar that isn't Google? Apple, Outlook and the rest can all export a .ics file — bring one in and the appointments land on the right people, repeat events and cancellations included. You can save yours out as a file too.
