label: v159
changes: Every folder you export now carries a proper PDF summary, not just a text file. A clinic, a school or an insurer opens it and sees a laid-out document — headings, tables, page numbers — instead of a screenful of asterisks and pipe characters.
The plain-text version still goes in too. That's the one another AI, a spreadsheet or a script reads cleanly, so you don't have to choose which end you're sending it to.
Both are written from the same records, so they can never disagree with each other.

label: v158
changes: Ask the assistant for a folder and it gathers one. "Prepare a folder with all Mia's medical reports and results" pulls her medical record, vaccinations, every referral and result, appointments, check-ups, growth and her doctors into one place — with the actual files, not just a list of them.

It isn't only medical. Ask for a school folder, her passport and visas for a visa appointment, or everything about someone so you can hand it to another AI — you name what it's for and it collects what fits.
You see exactly what's in it before anything leaves your phone: every topic listed with a real count, so "nothing on file" never hides behind a missing section. Tick things off or add them.

Then Share it straight into Mail, WhatsApp or another app, or download it as one zip. A written summary travels with the files so whoever opens it can read what they're looking at. If it's too big to email, it says so rather than letting you find out from a bounce.

label: v157
changes: Appointments for your children now show up under your children. Anything imported from Google Calendar arrived tagged to nobody — Google doesn't know who lives in your house — so "Ben – Orthodontist" sat on the calendar and appeared on nobody's Check-ups or Medical screen. The app now reads the name in the title and files it under that person.
It works on everything already in your calendar, not just new imports, so the appointments that were missing are there now without you doing anything.
Where a person was worked out from the title rather than tagged by hand, it says so. If it ever guesses wrong, open the event and assign it properly — your choice always wins from then on.

label: v156
changes: Fixed the thing that was quietly duplicating your calendar. Nothing checked whether an event was already there, so asking the assistant for the same appointment twice, or photographing the same school notice twice, added it again. That's how four identical "Re-test Ferritin and Vitamin D" entries appeared. Now it recognises the same appointment — same day, same time, same name — and tells you it's already there instead.

Importing from Google no longer brings in two copies of the same thing. It was only checking Google's internal id, so a repeating appointment that had been moved once arrived twice, looking identical. Six pairs of your "Klara" entries came in that way.
You already have 9 duplicate entries from before this fix. They're listed and waiting for you to say the word — nothing gets deleted without you.

label: v155
changes: Appointments now show up on the person they're for. Open someone's Check-ups and you see what they actually have booked — date, time, "next week" — and Medical shows the next few too. Before this, an appointment you added by voice went to the shared calendar and appeared nowhere on that person's own profile, which looked exactly like the app having lost it.
It's the same appointment in both places, not a copy. Change it on the calendar and it's right everywhere at once — nothing to keep in step, nothing to go stale.
The Check-ups screen used to call two different things "Appointments": real bookings, and rules like "dentist every six months". The recurring ones are now called Recurring check-ups.
The assistant is now told to always tag the person an appointment is for. It usually did, but nothing required it — and an untagged appointment is one that won't appear on anybody's profile.

label: v154
changes: The real fix: on a phone, tapping ANY section in the menu closed the menu and left you on the home screen. Calendar was just where you noticed it. The panel slides up over the page, and the code that closes it when you tap outside was counting taps INSIDE it as outside — so it shut itself before your tap could land on the section you'd chosen. It never happened on a laptop, where that panel is built differently. Now every section opens.
Sections also open at the top now, instead of keeping the scroll position from wherever you were.
The chat message box is now full width, on its own line, and grows as you type instead of being a two-character slot squeezed between the buttons.

The camera button in chat now just takes a photo. Scanning a document — finding the edges and straightening it — has its own button next to it, so you can pick the one you actually want instead of the camera always meaning "scan".

label: v153
changes: Fixed: tapping Calendar on a phone looked like nothing happened. It was opening — but the page stayed scrolled exactly where you'd left the family list, so you landed near the bottom of the calendar instead of the top of it. Every section now opens at the top. This is why it worked on the laptop and not on the phone.
The chat message box is now full width, on its own line, and grows as you type instead of being a two-character slot squeezed between the buttons.

The camera button in chat now just takes a photo. Scanning a document — finding the edges and straightening it — has its own button next to it, so you can pick the one you actually want instead of the camera always meaning "scan".

label: v152
changes: Important fix: "Export all events" pushed EVERY event to Google Calendar — including the hundreds it had originally imported from Google — so one tap would have filled your calendar with duplicates of your own appointments. It now only ever sends events created in Teluva, and events it can't safely send no longer show a button at all.

Appointments you add in Teluva can now appear on your phone automatically. It's off until you switch it on, in Calendar under Google Calendar sync, and it only ever sends events created after you turn it on — never your existing history.

Creating an invite now warns you first: while Teluva is in testing, Google only lets in people who have been added by name, so send Rory the Gmail address before you share the link. The shared message says the same thing, in case they hit Google's wall before they ever see our screen.

New in Wills & estate: "Who takes over" — name the person who should look after all this, and what you'd want them to do. It tells you honestly whether that person can actually sign in today, or whether you still need to make them an admin.

Also new there: where the keys, safes and deeds are, a letter in your own words for whoever finds it, who must be told, and the accounts to close — with tick boxes, so it doubles as a checklist for them.

You can now tell the assistant all of that out loud — "if something happens to me, tell my sister and cancel Netflix, the safe key is behind the wardrobe" — and it files it. It had no way to write to those fields before.
Fixed before it could bite: saving a will could have silently wiped the emergency instructions kept alongside it.
Empty sections no longer just say "nothing yet" in whatever style each screen happened to use — they now tell you what belongs there and give you the button to add the first one.
Lists that are still loading show the shape of what's coming instead of a spinning circle.
The avatar ring was Instagram's story-ring gradient, magenta and all. It's now our own warm one.
The Privacy, Terms and celebration pop-ups animate in like every other panel, and buttons respond to a tap on a phone rather than only to a mouse hovering.

The sign-in screen now warns you about Google's "hasn't verified this app" screen before you hit it, and tells you exactly what to tap. It also says you can use Teluva on a laptop, and what we do to keep your documents safe.

label: v149
changes: The update notice was showing you v138's notes on every release since — the changelog file was hand-written and hadn't been updated in ten deploys. The build now refuses to start if it goes stale again.

Scanned referrals, lab results, X-ray requests and sick notes now file into Referrals & Results on the person's Medical tab — not just into Documents. Repeat results of the same test group together as a history you can open by date.
Vaccination cards and visas/residence permits can now be filed from a photo too. All three were invisible to the assistant before, which is why scans kept landing in the wrong place.
You can delete or amend any of those by voice now — including marking a referral as booked or done.
Reminders now cover passports, residence permits and check-ups, and tomorrow's diary the night before. They arrive at 90, 30, 7 and 0 days — never daily — and as one message, not one per item.
New Emergency readiness card: it works out what's missing from what you've already saved, rather than asking you to fill in a survey. Every gap taps through to the screen that fixes it.
There's finally a field to type an emergency contact — until now only the assistant could set one.
Fun photo lab: pick a ready-made style and it generates in the background, so you can close it and carry on. It tells you when it's ready.
Scrolling on the dimmed area behind a pop-up no longer drags the page underneath.
A new Security tab (next to Privacy and Terms) says plainly what Teluva can and cannot see. Worth a read.
Connecting Google Drive no longer asks permission to delete your files, and Calendar no longer asks to manage all your calendars.

label: v138
changes: Fixed the big one: on an iPhone you couldn't reach the Apply button to accept the assistant's changes. The panel was sized against Safari's tallest possible screen, so its bottom sat behind the browser bar — nothing you could scroll to, because it was off-screen entirely. Every pop-up in the app had the same flaw and all of them are fixed.
Nothing was ever lost when that happened: changes are only saved when you tap Apply, and un-applied ones stay in the chat.
And now they come and find you — a bar on the home screen says how many changes are waiting, and opens them.
Long lists of changes start collapsed, so the Apply button is always the first thing you can reach rather than the last.
Android: long-press the app icon for Emergency card and Babysitter mode.

Star-sign blurbs read like a person now, not a fortune cookie. They were being told to paint the sky and the mood of the hour you were born — that instruction is gone, along with "cosmic", "the universe", "energy", "destined" and the rest. They're concrete and observational instead, flaws included, which is what stops them sounding like they'd fit anyone.

A family status — one line at the top of the home screen for whatever's happening right now. "Everyone at Oma's until Sunday." "Mia has chickenpox, don't visit." It shows who wrote it and when. It replaces rather than piles up, so it stays something you read at a glance instead of another feed to keep up with. Business spaces get it too.
Fixed: tapping the family photo opened the menu instead of the photo. That was my mistake when the header was rebuilt. It opens the photo again.
The family photo in the header is bigger.

The sections menu is grouped now — Everyday, Documents & IDs, Money & cover, Home & things, Memories — with Family and Emergency pinned at the top. Twenty-one sections in one flat list meant you had to already know the app to find anything.
On a phone it opens as a full sheet instead of a small panel with a hidden cap, so you can see there's more below rather than having to guess.
And there's a search box at the top of it: type three letters instead of reading the whole list.
